headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because aci has broad network egress and CRM/email access while caveman uses MCP and writes project files, creating unsafe cross-agent data flow by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest content from email/Slack/CRM and act via direct function calls or MCP, while caveman uses MCP and writes CLAUDE.md/project notes. That creates a plausible instruction-bridging path if caveman content is fed into aci or vice versa. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF caveman content is copied into aci prompts or MCP payloads, injected instructions can propagate.
IF aci ingests untrusted email/CRM text and caveman later treats it as guidance, prompt injection becomes viable.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces.
Disable MCP bridging between the two agents.
Add a manual review step for any text copied from one agent to the other.
Use allowlisted templates for prompts and file writes.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci has broad network egress and touches email, CRM, calendar, and support data; caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md. If they share a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive data can flow from aci into caveman outputs, and aci can exfiltrate via network. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or copied notes, aci data can enter caveman files.
IF caveman content is forwarded into aci's networked integrations, session or project data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep aci and caveman on separate directories.
Do not paste CRM/email content into caveman notes.
Turn off any automatic sync from caveman files into aci inputs.
Review outbound destinations for aci before enabling it.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and aci can write through APIs while caveman writes local files like CLAUDE.md and project notes. Overlapping mutable surfaces create conflict risk if they target the same project state, though no direct lockless git/database write is documented. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same project files or shared API-backed records, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF aci writes CRM or docs updates while caveman edits the same notes, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate write target.
Serialize edits with a human-approved queue.
Use read-only mode for one agent during the other's write window.
Snapshot files before running either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, and caveman can write project notes and CLAUDE.md that other tools may treat as authoritative. If caveman consumes aci-produced text without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or documentation. Because aci has action-taking authority, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF caveman uses aci output as source text without verification, incorrect facts can be propagated.
IF aci acts on caveman-generated summaries, mistaken instructions can trigger external side effects.
mitigations: Require source links before either agent acts on the other's output.
Add a human approval step for emails, calendar changes, and CRM updates.
Mark caveman notes as draft-only until reviewed.
Compare outputs against original records before execution.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches customer support, CRM, email, and calendar data, while caveman stores session logs, memory files, and project notes. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different retention-sensitive data classes and logging surfaces. That creates a plausible compliance gap if the same regulated data is shared across them.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied into caveman logs or notes, retention and subject-rights handling may diverge.
IF aci processes EU or PHI-like records through its external integrations, compliance review is required before sharing with caveman.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of caveman notes.
Minimize what aci sends to external services.
Document retention rules for both agents.
Review whether any shared data class has deletion/export obligations.
requires-engineering: align retention and access-control policies.
